nodes.name: FeCoW/NF Electrodeposition
nodes.procedure: A constant cathode potential is applied at -1.5 V vs saturated Ag/AgCl for 600s in a three-electrode system with a mixed aqueous solution containing sodium tungstate dihydrate, cobalt sulfate heptahydrate, sodium citrate dihydrate, ferrous sulfate heptahydrate, and boric acid. In this procedure, the boric acid is employed as a buffer. The sodium citrate dihydrate is a coordination agent for the electrodeposition of FeCoW hydroxides on the surface of nickel foam, which is beneficial to form stable complexes with metal ions, resulting in reducing the metal deposition rate. The lower pH, the more intense HER reaction, leading to lower current efficiency; therefore, the pH of mixed solution is adjusted to 4.0 using sulfuric acid. More experimental detailed description of the fabricating process of FeCoW/NF catalyst is provided in Supporting Information.

nodes.source_text: The FeCoW/NF electrocatalyst was fabricated using a one-step potentiostatic-electrodeposition. A constant cathode potential is applied at -1.5 V vs saturated Ag/AgCl for 600s in a three-electrode system with a mixed aqueous solution containing sodium tungstate dihydrate, cobalt sulfate heptahydrate, sodium citrate dihydrate, ferrous sulfate heptahydrate, and boric acid (Fig. S1). In this procedure, the boric acid is employed as a buffer. The sodium citrate dihydrate is a coordination agent for the electrodeposition of FeCoW hydroxides on the surface of nickel foam... the pH of mixed solution is adjusted to 4.0 using sulfuric acid.

nodes.characterization_summary: FeCoW/NF shows abundant vertically packed well-defined sheets with excellent uniformity and thickness of approximately 530 nm rooted on Ni foam surfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: After the introduction of W precursor... abundant vertically packed well-defined sheets of the FeCoW hydroxides with excellent uniformity and thickness of approximately 530 nm are rooted on the Ni foam surfaces (Fig. 1c, f and Fig. S2).

properties.description: High-resolution image showing microstructure with branched, porous morphology and rough surfaces

nodes.characterization_summary: The crystal structure of FeCoW/NF matches well with that of Ni foam (PDF#04-0850) due to low contents of FeCoW on NF surface.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As exhibited in Fig. 2a... the crystal structure of the as-synthesized FeCoW/NF catalyst matches well with that of Ni foam (PDF#04e0850).

nodes.characterization_summary: FeCoW/NF shows sheet-like structure with lattice fringe spacings of 0.20 nm and 0.24 nm corresponding to CoFe-LDH crystal planes (018) and (012), respectively.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In the high-resolution TEM image of FeCoW/NF catalyst, the lattice fringe spacings of 0.20 nm and 0.24 nm correspond to CoFe-LDH crystal planes (018) and (012), respectively.

properties.description: Granular nanostructure with scale bar 5 nm

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM mapping images show homogeneous distribution of Fe, Co, W and O elements in FeCoW/NF catalyst.
nodes.evidence_snippet: TEM mapping images of the FeCoW/NF catalyst show that Fe, Co, W and O distributions are identical to those in SEM, as indicated by the X-ray energy dispersive spectrometer (EDS) images.

nodes.characterization_summary: Molar ratio of Fe, Co and W in FeCoW/NF is approximately 7:5:1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Based the results of inductively coupled plasma optical emission spectrometry (ICP-OES), the molar ratio of Fe, Co and W is approximately estimated to be 7:5:1.

nodes.characterization_summary: FeCoW/NF XPS shows Fe2+ (711.0 eV 2p3/2, 724.4 eV 2p1/2), Fe3+ (713.3, 726.1 eV); Co2+ (782.3, 797.9 eV), Co3+ (780.7, 796.6 eV); W6+ (35.4 eV 4f7/2, 37.5 eV 4f5/2); O 1s at 529.7 eV (M-O), 531.3 eV (M-OH), 532.5 eV (H2Oad) confirming FeCoW hydroxide formation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The above XPS analyses confirm the successful formation of FeCoW hydroxides on the FeCoW/NF surface, which is in accordance with TEM result.
